3.OBSTETRIC CHOLESTASIS:

Definition:

Itching over normal looking skin + raised bile aids during pregnancy (especially 3rd trimester) returning to normal after 4 weeks of delivery (LFT’s & B.A + itching).

Prevalence:

•OC:
-0.7% overall.
-1.2 – 1.5% Asian (Pakistani, Indian).
•Itching in pregnancy 25%.

 

Association of itching is with LFT’S.

Association of still birth is with Bile acids.

Diagnosis:

•Itching + raised Bile Acid > 19mmol/ lit + normalization after birth.
•ICP can co – exist with eczema.
•No need of fasting B.A (Bile Acids)
•Use pregnancy specific ranges for LFT’S.

D/D:

1.Gestational Pruritis= Normal B.A.

OC can develop up to 15 weeks after Gestational pruritis.

2.Pre – Eclampsia.
3.Eczema, allergic reactions.
4.Viral illness.

Indications of involvement of Hepatologist & Other Tests i.e., lab tests, imaging.

Are recommended if:

1.Early onset OC (1st or 2nd trimester).
2.Atypical presentation.
3.Co – morbidities present.
4.Delayed or no resolution items & B.A after birth.

Maternal Risks:

•Itching affecting sleep and mental health.
•Pre – eclampsia 12.2% (vs 3.4% background risk).
•Gest diabetes 13.2% (vs 5.9% background risk ).

Other symptoms:

•Dark urine.
•Pale stools.
•Steatorrhea.
•Malabsorption of Vitamin K 1%.

Fetal Risks:

1.Still birth – depends upon levels of B.A (No association with ALT).
1.19 – 39 mmol/lit = No additional risk of S.B.
2.40 – 99 similar to background till 38 weeks.
3.> 100uml/lit high risk of S.B.

OC + G.DM or

OC + PE or higher risk of S.B

OC + Multiple

Pregnancy

Raised Bile Acid cause anoxia due to arrhythmia or placental vascular spasm.

 

2.Pre – Term Birth (spontaneous/ iatrogenic)

Moderate or severe OC.

3.Meconium stained Amniotic Fluid.

Moderate or severe OC.

4.Neonatal care.

Moderate or severe.

 

Antenatal Care:

⇨Consultant led care
•Monitoring of B.P.
•Review of blood sugar levels.
•Repeating B.A: initially after 1 week later depending on condition or subsequent Test reports:
-Rising.
-Falling.
-Fluctuating.

Fetal Monitoring:

•CTG or USG => don’t predict or prevent S.B.
•Advice women to monitor fetal movement and report to maternity units if concern arises.
•No role of Doppler as:

Fetus don’t have IUGR or Placental insufficiency.

Treatment:

•No drug can itching, B.A, fetal problems.
•Topical emollients:

Aqueous cream with or without menthol skin symptoms.

•Anti-Histamine:

Chlorpheniramine @ night – can be used but effectiveness is uncertain.

•Ursodeoxycholic Acid:
-Don’t regularly offer to reduce adverse perinatal outcome like S.B.
-Reduce pre – Term birth.
-No effect on itching.
•Rifampicin – under trial.
•Vitamin K indicated if there is
1.Steatorrhea.
2.Abnormal PT.
-10mg/ day.
-Water soluble.

Timing of Birth:

•Mild – 40 weeks or beyond.
•Moderate – 38 – 39 weeks.
•Severe – 35 – 36 weeks.
•OC + Comorbidities = affect timing of birth.

Mode of Birth:

OC is not an indication of C/section.

MOD depends upon obstetric indication.

Fetal Monitoring:

•CEFM = severe obstetric cholestasis.
•Presence of risk factors with OC is also indication of CEFM.

Routine monitoring in mild OC.

•In moderate OC monitoring depends on individual circumstances.

Analgesia in labor:

Standard analgesia + Anesthesia.

3rd Stage:

•Standard care.
•No ed risk of PPH.

Follow Up:

⇨After 4 weeks:
•itching should stop
•LFT’s and B.A should turn to normal in order to confirm diagnosis.

Contraception:

UKMEC category 1

•CU – T
•POP
•Implanon.
•Mirena.

UKMEC category 2

OCP: Avoid in women with OC with OCP’S and Atypical OC.

Atypical OC: Personalized options.

Recurrence in future pregnancies and Care:

•Risk of recurrence.

LFT’S and B.A @ booking in subsequent pregnancies.
